title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This sits inside the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript, the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type material that continues La Longue Marche. N_{1,1}^~ is a group of automorphisms acting on the profinite fundamental group of the modular stack M_{1,1}. That group is SL(2,Z)^, topologically generated by rho (order 6) and sigma (order 4), with rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1.

Previous page. Each u in N_{1,1}^~ has a multiplier mu = chi(u) in Zhat^*, a cyclotomic-type character. Its image in GL(2,Zhat) is diag(mu,1). Its action on the generators is u(rho) = int(alpha~)(rho) = xi·rho and u(sigma) = eps·int(beta~)(sigma) = eta·sigma. Here xi = alpha~·rho(alpha~)^{-1} and eta = eps·beta~·sigma(beta~)^{-1}, where rho(alpha~) means rho·alpha~·rho^{-1}. So xi·rho = alpha~ rho alpha~^{-1}, which is a cocycle-style normalisation as in the (lambda,f) description of GT. The sign is eps = eps_2(mu) = ±1 according as mu ≡ ±1 mod 4.

This page, step by step.
1. alpha~ and beta~ are arbitrary lifts. Since -1 is central they are defined only up to sign, but int(alpha~), int(beta~), and hence xi and eta, are well defined.
2. Also recorded: u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu, where eps_0 = sigma·rho is the parabolic generator (the 'loop at infinity'). This is the usual cyclotomic action on inertia at the cusp.
3. A homomorphism Psi: N_{1,1}^~ → G is then considered. Its restriction to the geometric part gives a surjection SL(2,Z)^ ↠ 𝔾 = Im ⊂ G.
4. In any such quotient the images still satisfy rho^6 = sigma^4 = 1 and rho^3 = sigma^2. Hence [rho^3, sigma] = [sigma^2, rho] = 1, so rho^3 = sigma^2 is central. Thus every quotient 𝔾 carries a canonical central element of order ≤2, written -1.
5. For u in N_{1,1}^~(omega) one pushes xi and eta into 𝔾, obtaining xi_𝔾 and eta_𝔾 with u_𝔾(rho_𝔾) = xi_𝔾·rho_𝔾 and u_𝔾(sigma_𝔾) = eta_𝔾·sigma_𝔾 (formula 23).
6. The next page explains why this is not quite enough. alpha~ need only lie in GL(2,Zhat), not SL(2,Zhat), so the orientation-reversing element tau must be adjoined. tau acts by tau(sigma) = sigma^{-1}, tau(rho) = sigma(rho^{-1}), and one forms the semidirect product {1,tau}⋉𝔾.

Purpose. The aim is to transport the GT/Galois action on pi_1(M_{1,1}) to arbitrary finite (or profinite) quotients 𝔾. These correspond to dessins / finite covers of the modular curve, possibly non-congruence ones. The pair (xi_𝔾, eta_𝔾) serves as the computable data of the action. Grothendieck then says he will 'paraphrase constructions already made elsewhere', i.e. the genus-0 analogue with the lacets equation.
errors: The transcription's formula 'u(rho)= int(alpha~)(rho) = xi rho' with xi = alpha~ rho alpha~^{-1} would be inconsistent. It is consistent only if rho(alpha~) is read as rho·alpha~·rho^{-1}, which is what the notation means. No mathematical error on the page itself.
Equation number (20) is used twice on the page: once for u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu and once for Psi. This is a numbering slip only.
Minor point: in a quotient 𝔾 the element 'rho^3 = sigma^2' may be trivial, so '-1' is involutive or trivial. Grothendieck's 'involutif' should be read as '(-1)^2 = 1'.

ideas.what: Presentation SL(2,Z)^ = <rho, sigma | rho^6 = sigma^4 = 1, rho^3 = sigma^2>, with rho^3 = sigma^2 central and giving a canonical central involution -1 in every quotient
ideas.modern_name: amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and its profinite completion

ideas.what: Writing the action of a GT-type automorphism u on SL(2,Z)^ as u(rho) = xi·rho, u(sigma) = eta·sigma, with xi, eta independent of the sign ambiguity of the lifts and a sign eps_2(mu) depending on mu mod 4
ideas.modern_name: GT / Galois action on the profinite mapping class group of M_{1,1} (genus-one, one-point level of the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu for the parabolic eps_0 = sigma·rho
Pushing the action data to arbitrary finite quotients 𝔾 of SL(2,Z)^ (finite covers of M_{1,1}) and adjoining the orientation reversal tau via the semidirect product {1,tau}⋉𝔾
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on finite-index subgroups of SL(2,Z) (modular dessins); extension to GL(2) by complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schneps and others on GT and dessins; Belyi-type modular curves literature

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine setup of the GT-type action on SL(2,Z)^ and its quotients, fixing sign conventions. The material is known in substance from the later genus-one GT literature (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps), even though this precise private formulation is unpublished. No new result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'relèvements arbitraires de alpha et beta dans SL(2,Z)^' (the transcription has ':' where the image reads 'dans' or similar).
The insertion above 'mais xi et eta...' reads 'int(alpha~), int(beta~),', not 'mod(alpha~), mod(beta~)'. That is: 'mais int(alpha~), int(beta~), xi et eta sont déterminés sans ambiguïté'.
'pour u. (20)' is probably 'pour u ∈ N_{1,1}^~' preceding u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu.
Under (21) the annotation reads '= Im Psi', i.e. 𝔾 is the image of SL(2,Z)^ under Psi.
Margin note: 'donc dans 𝔾 il y a un élément central canonique involutif, noté -1'.
Last line: 'et faire jouer pareil sur alpha~ et beta~. Mais on [est obligé...]'.
The '507' at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination; the archive page is 527.
